interest: A Depression-era Ohio fruit grower asks whether Japan banned labor-displacing machinery.
overview: This file (decimal file 894.044) covers records of the U.S. Department of State relating to the judicial branch, laws, statutes, and decrees of Japan from January 1933 to April 1939. The primary document cluster from January 1933 concerns a constituent inquiry from H. Burkholder, an Ohio fruit farmer, forwarded by Senator Simeon D. Fess to Stanley K. Hornbeck, Chief of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs, asking whether Japan had enacted legislation prohibiting the introduction of labor-displacing machinery during the Depression. The State Department consulted Japanese experts and the Legal Adviser, concluding that no such laws likely existed, but noting that the Department did not keep comprehensive collections of foreign laws and referring Burkholder to the International Labor Office in Washington. The file also includes an April 1939 cross-reference sheet indexing a Tokyo embassy despatch from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew that transmitted a translation of Japan's Law for the Protection of Secrets of Resources for Military Use.
